claims.reason: 1.1 gives the count (sattime ... bojjhaṅgā) and 1.3 names satisambojjhaṅgo and upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo; the middle five rest on the conventional expansion of '…pe…' in the Pali (Sujato's English spells all seven out).

1.1 and 1.4: bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā, a necessary (not sufficient) condition, which 'is required for' captures; the wording is verbatim from 1.1 and the note correctly restores 'unarisen' (anuppannā), which Sujato's English drops.

texts.notes: Sujato's English omits anuppannā ('unarisen'); the claim's note and the coverage record both restore it. The list's middle five members depend on '…pe…' in 1.3; the list node carries no note saying so (same in every text in this batch).

claims.reason: 1.1 gives the count and 1.3 names the first and last (satisambojjhaṅgo …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo); the middle five rest on the conventional expansion.
1.1 and 1.4: bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā, a necessary condition fairly encoded as 'is required for'; the wording is verbatim from 1.1 English.

texts.notes: The uddāna (2.0-2.4) lists the chapter's titles and is rightly treated as non-teaching. As in SN 46.9, the English omits anuppannā; c-u2's note refers back to c-u1's note, which covers it.

claims.reason: 2.3-2.7 name kāmacchanda, byāpāda, thinamiddha, uddhaccakukkucca and vicikicchā in full in the Pali, and 2.1 gives the count pañca.
3.1 gives the count and 3.3 names satisambojjhaṅgo and upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo in full; the middle five rest on the conventional expansion of '…pe…'.

3.1, 3.3 and 3.4: bojjhaṅgā ... bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti; 'leads to' fairly renders saṁvattanti, though the subject drops the qualifier 'when developed and cultivated'.
2.1 and 2.8 (paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā), repeated for each hindrance in the Pali only at 2.3-2.7, as the coverage record says; direction and target are correct.

texts.notes: The left-out note correctly describes the parasitic-fig simile (1.1-1.4), its point at 1.5 (a renunciate overcome by sensual pleasures like those he gave up, or worse: tādisakehi kāmehi tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarehi), and the unmodelled 'not obstacles' statement in 3.1. Sujato's English at 2.3-2.7 gives only the names; the Pali repeats the full predicate for each, as the coverage record notes. o-12's subject leaves out bhāvitā bahulīkatā ('when developed and cultivated'); that is acceptable under the summary-may-simplify rule but worth keeping in mind.

claims.reason: 2.1 gives the count (sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṁ) and 2.3 names the first and last; the middle five rest on the conventional expansion of '…pe…'.

2.1 and 2.4: tathāgatassa pātubhāvā ... sattannaṁ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṁ pātubhāvo hoti; 'when present, then ... arise' fairly renders the ablative, the wording is verbatim from 2.1, and the note says the text calls them 'treasures' (ratana), so this appearance is of the factors as treasures in the world.

1.1-1.4 (cakkavattissa pātubhāvā sattannaṁ ratanānaṁ pātubhāvo) are set in exact parallel to 2.1; the image and the point are the text's, and the note openly says the text has no seyyathāpi/evameva markers, so classing it as a simile is the modellers' disclosed choice.

texts.notes: The text has only the monarch parallel and the Tathāgata statement, and both are encoded, so 'fully encoded' holds. Calling the parallel a 'simile' is a modelling decision (D23); the text itself only juxtaposes the two.

claims.reason: 23.1 gives the count and 23.3 names the first and last in full; the middle five rest on the conventional expansion of '…pe…'.

In 3.1 and 4.3 the condition is two things together, the mind obsessed and overcome by kāmarāga (kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena) and not truly understanding the escape (nissaraṇaṁ yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti); the structured fields reduce this to 'sensual lust when present', and the full condition appears only in the wording and note.

In 5.1 and 6.3 the condition is a mind obsessed by byāpāda plus not understanding the escape, but the fields say only 'ill will when present'; the note is also wrong to say 'for both' is abbreviated, since ubhayatthampi tasmiṁ samaye yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati is given in full in both segments (only paratthampi is abbreviated).

In 7.1 and 8.3 the condition is a mind obsessed by thinamiddha plus not understanding the escape, reduced in the fields to 'when present'; as with c-g2, the note wrongly says 'for both' is abbreviated, when ubhayattha is given in full in 7.1 and 8.3.

In 9.1 and 10.3 the condition is a mind obsessed by uddhaccakukkucca plus not understanding the escape, reduced in the fields to 'when present'; the note wrongly says 'for both' is abbreviated, when ubhayattha is given in full in 9.1 and 10.3.

In 11.1 and 12.3 the condition is a mind obsessed by vicikicchā plus not understanding the escape, reduced in the fields to 'when present' (the note gives it in full); the Pali wording matches 11.1, and 12.3 supplies para/ubhaya in full.
23.1, 23.3 and 23.4: bojjhaṅgā ... bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti; the subject drops 'when developed and cultivated', a fair simplification.

6.1-6.3: the water is agginā santatto pakkuthito, a clear-eyed man cannot see his reflection as it is, and 'evameva' ties it to byāpāda; the wording is verbatim 6.3 English (the English elides with '…' where the Pali continues).
4.1-4.3: water mixed with lākhā, haliddī, nīlī or mañjiṭṭhā, no true reflection, and 'evameva' ties it to kāmarāga; the image, point and mapping are the text's.
8.1-8.3: sevālapaṇakapariyonaddho, mapped by 'evameva' to thinamiddha; correct image and target.
12.1-12.3: āvilo luḷito kalalībhūto andhakāre nikkhitto, mapped to vicikicchā; the wording is verbatim from 12.3 English, which is complete here.
10.1-10.3: vāterito calito bhanto ūmijāto, mapped to uddhaccakukkucca; correct image and target.

texts.notes: Every teaching section is either encoded or named in the left-out note (reverse teaching 13.1-22.4, hymns 2.1-2.2/12.4/22.4, 'not obstacles' 23.1, frame 1.1-1.3/24.1-24.3). Small inaccuracy: the left-out note says the hymns consequence is 'kept in the claims' notes', but only c-g1 and c-g5 mention it; c-g2 to c-g4 do not (the similes' wording does). The condition label 'sensual lust' correctly follows the Pali kāmarāga rather than Sujato's 'sensual desire'. Sujato's English at 4.3, 5.1-11.1 elides with '…' while the Pali continues; c-g2 to c-g4 rightly quote the Pali instead. The c-g STRETCH verdicts are minor because the summary and wording carry the full two-part condition; only the structured condition field is narrowed.
